description.en: Lesson 2.1 Cortisol on the skin · Lesson 2.2 Estrogen, menopause and collagen · Lesson 2.3 Skin signs that need an endocrinologist.

units.tutorContext: Module 2 separates local hormonal skin biology from systemic endocrine disease and keeps four registers apart (mechanism, human evidence, regulatory status, open question). Cortisol: skin expresses an HPA-like axis (CRH, POMC/ACTH) and regenerates cortisol via 11β-HSD1 in keratinocytes and fibroblasts; activity higher in aged and photo-exposed skin, set independently of blood levels (mechanism, D). Only human 11β-HSD1 skin RCT: 28-person pilot in type 2 diabetes, primary outcome missed, exploratory faster wound closure (C); investigational, no FDA approval, no skin-ageing trial registered (24 Sep 2026). Endocrine Society 2008: best discriminators of Cushing's = easy bruising, facial plethora, proximal myopathy, reddish-purple striae >1 cm; facial fullness, dorsocervical fat pad, weight gain, acne, hirsutism, fatigue are common/less discriminating; drug history first (incl. skin-bleaching creams, injections); endogenous incidence 2–3 per million/yr; commonest cause iatrogenic; test multiple progressive features; against widespread testing and random serum cortisol; abnormal → endocrinologist. Estrogen: ERα/ERβ/GPER in skin; topical estradiol raises collagen in sun-protected not photoaged skin (D); collagen and thickness fall ~1–2%/yr after menopause tracking years since menopause (D; the guide's '30% in 5 years' is a review figure not found in primary abstracts). Systemic HT: small RCTs raise skin thickness/collagen (C); largest RCT (n=485, 48 wk) and 4-year KEEPS found no wrinkle difference (B); guide grades B, NAMS Level II, course C for structural gains. US (Feb 2026): MHT approved for hot flashes, vulvovaginal/GSM symptoms, bone loss (some products); 2025–26 label changes removed CV/breast/dementia statements from boxed warning; skin never an indication. NAMS 2022: favourable <60 or within 10 years for symptoms/bone; compounded bioidentical HT insufficient evidence. OTC 'hormone creams' = unapproved drugs (21 CFR 310.530). Skin care with better evidence: daily sunscreen (RCT n=903, B); tretinoin cream FDA-approved adjunct for fine wrinkles. Red flags → referral, never diagnosis by the aesthetic clinician: rapid hirsutism/virilization (tumour ~0.2%, >half malignant) urgent; generalised hyperpigmentation in creases/scars/mucosa with illness (adrenal insufficiency) urgent; Cushing's discriminators, MEN1 angiofibromas (88% of MEN1, not in tuberous sclerosis), Carney complex (lip/eyelid/canthal lentigines, blue naevi, myxomas; cardiac myxomas >50% of deaths), MEN2A interscapular lichen amyloidosis (RET 634) → endocrine referral. Never give doses, regimens or product sourcing; adapt 'what you do next' to prescriber, clinical staff or advisor without changing facts. No CME credit is currently offered.

learningObjectives.en: Distinguish between pathological hypercortisolemia and local 11β-HSD1 glucocorticoid activity in patients presenting with facial adiposity and cutaneous barrier breakdown.
Critique the human clinical evidence evaluating systemic and topical estrogen on dermal thickness, wound healing, and postmenopausal collagen decline.
Identify pathognomonic dermatologic signs of underlying endocrine diseases (e.g., Carney complex, Cushing's, thyroid dysfunction) requiring specialist referral rather than cosmetic intervention.

lead.en: Module 02 · Hormones written on the skin

title.en: The face that might be a diagnosis.

body.en: Most skin changes you see are ageing or lifestyle. A few are the first visible sign of endocrine disease. In three lessons you will separate them: what local and systemic hormones do to skin, what hormone therapy can and cannot do for it, and which signs belong with an endocrinologist.

points.en: 2.1 Cortisol on the skin: local 11β-HSD1 and Cushing's syndrome
2.2 Estrogen, menopause and collagen: what the trials show
2.3 Skin signs that need an endocrinologist

blocks.sourceNote: Hormones and Peptides for Skin · Module 02

title.en: The skin regenerates its own cortisol.

body.en: Skin expresses the machinery of a local stress axis, including CRH and POMC with its product ACTH. Keratinocytes and dermal fibroblasts also carry 11β-HSD1, the enzyme that turns inactive cortisone back into active cortisol inside the cell. In human skin samples its activity is higher with age and in sun-exposed skin, and local cortisol availability is set independently of blood levels. Cortisol slows collagen production in dermal fibroblasts, and mice lacking the enzyme kept their dermal thickness with age.

points.en: Local axis: CRH, POMC and ACTH are made in skin
11β-HSD1 regenerates cortisol inside skin cells
Mechanism register: human samples, cultured cells and mice

blocks.sourceNote: Slominski & Wortsman 2000 · Tiganescu 2011, 2013 · Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, ch. 8

body.en: Skin makes CRH and POMC-derived ACTH and carries their receptors, a field-restricted copy of the hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal axis.
11β-HSD1 converts cortisone to cortisol in keratinocytes and fibroblasts. In human skin samples its activity rises with age and with sun exposure.
Cortisol slows collagen synthesis in fibroblasts, and knockout mice kept their dermal thickness as they aged. Whether this drives visible ageing in people has not been tested.

audioScript.en: Picture the skin as a small endocrine organ with its own stress axis. Skin cells make CRH and ACTH, the same signals that drive the adrenal glands, and they carry the receptors to respond to them. They also carry an enzyme called eleven beta HSD one, which turns inactive cortisone back into active cortisol inside the cell. In human skin samples that enzyme works harder with age and in sun-exposed skin, and it sets local cortisol independently of the level in the blood. Cortisol slows collagen production in dermal fibroblasts, and mice bred without the enzyme kept their dermal thickness as they aged. Hold all of this in the mechanism register. It comes from biopsies, cultured cells and mice, and it says nothing yet about how a patient's face will age.

body.en: Local cortisol regeneration is a real and interesting mechanism. Each register below answers a different question, and blending them produces the line you will hear online: that blocking cortisol in the skin reverses ageing.

blocks.sourceNote: Tiganescu 2011, 2013 · Ajjan 2022 · ClinicalTrials.gov and Drugs@FDA, checked 24 Sep 2026

note.en: Enzyme activity rises with age and sun exposure in human skin samples; knockout mice resist age-related dermal thinning
28 adults with type 2 diabetes took an oral inhibitor: the primary outcome was missed, wounds closed faster in an exploratory analysis, and barrier function was modestly worse
The inhibitor tested in human skin is a research compound with no FDA approval
No registered trial tests an 11β-HSD1 inhibitor for skin ageing (ClinicalTrials.gov, 24 September 2026)

callout.en: Local cortisol is set inside the skin, so a blood, saliva or hair cortisol cannot read it.

body.en: Cushing's syndrome shares most of its features with ordinary weight gain, poor sleep and stress. The Endocrine Society's diagnostic guideline separates the few that discriminate from the many that are common. Before you see its verdicts, sort these eight.

blocks.sourceNote: Endocrine Society guideline, Nieman 2008, Table 1 · Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, ch. 8

note.en: Bruises without an obvious injury
A persistently red, full-blooded complexion
Trouble rising from a chair or climbing stairs
Reddish-purple and wider than 1 cm
A rounder face than a year ago
Gradual gain over several years
New or persistent
Tired, sleeping badly

callout.en: Few features of Cushing's syndrome are unique. Some discriminate far better than others.

prompt.en: Tap where each feature belongs.

why.en: One of the four features the guideline lists as best discriminating, particularly bruising with no obvious trauma.
Listed among the best discriminators. Most of the four have low sensitivity, so their absence does not exclude the syndrome.
Proximal myopathy is one of the four; ask about stairs and getting up from a low chair.
The guideline singles out striae that are reddish-purple and wider than 1 cm.
The guideline lists facial fullness, like the dorsocervical fat pad, among features that are common in the general population. A round face alone is a weak signal.
Common and less discriminatory on its own; many features of cortisol excess are shared with ordinary obesity.
Both sit on the guideline's common, less discriminatory list; persistent hirsutism more often points to androgen excess (lesson 2.3).
Fatigue, insomnia and poor concentration are common and less discriminatory.

done.en: Eight sorted. Four features discriminate: easy bruising, facial plethora, proximal weakness and wide reddish-purple striae. A round face on its own is a weak signal.

interaction.source: authored:2026-09-24 from Nieman 2008 Table 1 (Endocrine Society) + claim c-m02-03

title.en: Rare, and usually from a prescription.

body.en: Endogenous Cushing's syndrome is uncommon: European population studies put it at two to three new cases per million people a year. The commonest cause of Cushing's syndrome is iatrogenic, from glucocorticoids given as medicine. The Endocrine Society therefore asks for a drug history first, covering tablets, inhalers, injections and creams, including skin-bleaching products, and recommends testing when features are multiple and progressive.

blocks.sourceNote: Endocrine Society guideline, Nieman 2008 — introduction and recommendations 3.1–3.3

label.en: new cases of endogenous Cushing's syndrome per million people per year (European population studies)

detail.en: As cited in the Endocrine Society diagnostic guideline, 2008

means.en: A round, puffy face in an aesthetic clinic is almost always something other than Cushing's syndrome, and when cortisol excess is real it most often comes from a glucocorticoid the patient is already using.

doesNot.en: It does not mean you can dismiss it. The guideline recommends testing when discriminating features are multiple and progressive or unusual for age, and some groups, such as people with poorly controlled diabetes, carry a higher rate.

title.en: Reassure the many, refer the few.

body.en: When a patient asks about 'cortisol face', start with the drug history: steroid creams, skin-lighteners, herbal tonics and injections. Then look for the discriminating features. Without them, the Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide reads most puffiness as sleep, alcohol, salt and fluid, and the Endocrine Society recommends against widespread testing. With them, especially when they are progressing, the next step is formal testing and an endocrinologist. A cortisol supplement or a consumer cortisol panel answers the wrong question.

points.en: Drug history first, including creams and injections
Look for bruising, plethora, proximal weakness, wide purple striae
Refer for testing; skip supplements and consumer panels

blocks.sourceNote: Endocrine Society guideline 2008, recommendations 3.1–3.5 · Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, ch. 8 clinical pearl

body.en: Glucocorticoids hide in skin-bleaching creams, herbal tonics and joint or nerve injections. The guideline asks for that history before any cortisol test.
Easy bruising, a plethoric face, proximal weakness and wide reddish-purple striae are the features that shift the odds.
First-line tests are urine free cortisol, late-night salivary cortisol or an overnight dexamethasone suppression test, ordered by a prescriber; an abnormal result goes to an endocrinologist.

audioScript.en: Here is how that plays out when a patient asks about cortisol face. Begin with a drug history, because the commonest cause of cortisol excess is a glucocorticoid someone is already using. The guideline names the easy ones to miss, such as skin-bleaching creams, herbal tonics, and joint or nerve injections. Then look for the four features that shift the odds, meaning easy bruising, a plethoric face, weakness in the hips and shoulders, and wide reddish-purple striae. Without them, the Aesthetic and Regenerative Endocrinology guide reads most puffiness as sleep, alcohol, salt and fluid, and the Endocrine Society advises against testing everyone. With them, and especially when they are progressing, the patient needs formal testing and an endocrinologist. A cortisol supplement or a mail-order saliva panel answers the wrong question.

prescriber.en: If discriminating features are present, arrange one of the guideline's first-line tests or refer directly to endocrinology, and document the drug history, including creams and injections. An abnormal result goes to an endocrinologist.

clinical-staff.en: Record any steroid creams, skin-lighteners or injections the patient mentions, note bruising or wide purple striae you see, and bring it to the prescriber before the next treatment.

advisor.en: Do not recommend 'cortisol-lowering' supplements or consumer cortisol kits. If a patient describes easy bruising, muscle weakness or new wide purple stretch marks, point them to a prescriber.

body.en: One question to close lesson 2.1.

blocks.sourceNote: Lesson 2.1

prompt.en: A 38-year-old asks whether her puffy morning face is 'cortisol face'. She sleeps badly and drinks most evenings. What is the best next step?

text.en: Recommend a consumer saliva cortisol panel to check her levels.

why.en: Testing is for multiple, progressive discriminating features; the guideline advises against widespread testing and random cortisol measures, and the guide calls consumer panels poorly validated.

text.en: Take a drug history, including creams and injections, and examine for bruising, plethora, proximal weakness and wide purple striae; refer if they are present.

why.en: Correct. Exclude exogenous glucocorticoids, then look for the discriminating features before anyone orders a test.

text.en: Reassure her that Cushing's syndrome is too rare to consider.

why.en: It is rare, but the guideline asks you to consider it when discriminating features cluster; reassurance comes after the history and examination.

feedback.en: Drug history, discriminating features, then referral — in that order.

body.en: Skin carries estrogen receptors (ERα, ERβ and the membrane receptor GPER) in both sun-protected and sun-damaged sites. In postmenopausal women, two weeks of topical estradiol raised collagen production in sun-protected hip skin; photoaged facial skin showed no such response. After menopause, small biopsy studies found skin collagen and thickness falling year by year, following years since menopause more closely than age. That is mechanism and natural history. What hormone therapy does to a face is a separate question.

points.en: Receptors: ERα, ERβ and GPER in aged and photoaged skin
Topical estradiol raises collagen in sun-protected skin only
Collagen loss follows years since menopause

blocks.sourceNote: Rittié 2008 · Thornton 2013 · Brincat 1985 · Affinito 1999 · Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, ch. 9

body.en: Estrogen receptors are expressed in sun-protected and sun-damaged skin alike.

title.en: A collagen signal, with a limit

body.en: Two weeks of topical estradiol raised procollagen in the hip skin of postmenopausal women; in photoaged face and forearm skin it made no measurable difference.
In small biopsy studies, skin collagen fell with years since menopause more than with chronological age.

audioScript.en: Estrogen is the hormone the guide says dominates the visible ageing of women's skin, so start with what it does in the dermis. Skin carries estrogen receptors in sun-protected and sun-damaged sites alike. In a vehicle-controlled study, two weeks of topical estradiol raised collagen production in the hip skin of postmenopausal women; in photoaged forearm and facial skin, the same treatment made no measurable difference. Small biopsy studies from the nineteen eighties and nineties found that skin collagen and thickness fall after menopause, and that the fall follows years since the last period more closely than birthdays. Keep two questions apart as you go. One is what estrogen does in the dermis. The other is whether giving it changes how a face ages, and those answers come from different trials.

title.en: One to two per cent a year.

body.en: In small biopsy studies of postmenopausal women, skin collagen content and skin thickness fell by about 1–2% a year, in step with bone mass, and followed years since menopause more than age. Reviews, and the Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide, quote a steeper early loss of up to 30% in the first five years. That figure traces to the same small studies, and a check of their abstracts in September 2026 did not find it stated.

blocks.sourceNote: Brincat 1985, 1987 · Affinito 1999 · Thornton 2013

label.en: fall in skin collagen content and thickness per year after menopause (small biopsy studies)

detail.en: Brincat et al., 1987 — in parallel with bone mass

means.en: Estrogen withdrawal is a measurable contributor to dermal thinning, and it follows the menopause clock rather than age alone.

doesNot.en: It does not show that hormone therapy restores a younger-looking face. These are small observational studies, mostly of non-facial skin; the treatment trials come next.

body.en: Hormone therapy has two kinds of trial behind it. Small trials measure the dermis; larger trials measure the face. They point in different directions, so read them separately. The Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide grades the skin benefit B; the North American Menopause Society rates the same evidence 'limited or inconsistent'. This course grades the structural gains C and teaches the negative wrinkle trials alongside them.

blocks.sourceNote: Maheux 1994 · Sauerbronn 2000 · Phillips 2008 · Owen 2016 · Pivazyan 2023 · Creidi 1994 · Ashcroft 1999 · NAMS 2022

label.en: Systemic HT · skin thickness and collagen

note.en: Two small RCTs (60 and 41 women) measured hip and upper-arm skin
485 women for 48 weeks on low-dose therapy; a four-year trial in recently menopausal women also found no difference
Small studies, some non-randomized, varying widely; its authors do not propose hormone therapy as a skin treatment
One 24-week RCT improved thickness and fine lines; a biopsy study found no collagen response in photoaged facial skin
A small randomized study in healthy older adults

callout.en: A thicker dermis on biopsy and a younger-looking face are different outcomes. Ask which one a trial measured.

title.en: Symptoms and bone. Skin is a bystander.

body.en: In the US, as of February 2026, FDA-approved menopausal hormone therapy is for moderate-to-severe hot flashes, vaginal and vulvar symptoms and, for some products, preventing bone loss. FDA's 2025–26 labeling changes removed cardiovascular, breast-cancer and dementia statements from the boxed warning; skin did not become an indication. The North American Menopause Society's 2022 statement finds benefit outweighs risk for bothersome symptoms and bone protection when therapy starts before 60 or within 10 years of menopause, and finds insufficient evidence for compounded 'bioidentical' hormones. Under US rules an over-the-counter 'hormone cream' is an unapproved drug. For the skin itself, daily sunscreen has a large randomized trial behind it, and one tretinoin cream is FDA-approved as an adjunct for fine facial wrinkles.

points.en: Indications: hot flashes, genitourinary symptoms, bone
Low-dose vaginal estrogen for GSM: the one estrogen-for-tissue use
For the skin itself: daily sunscreen and a retinoid

blocks.sourceNote: FDA, 10 Nov 2025 and 12 Feb 2026 · 21 CFR 310.530 · NAMS 2022, 2020 · Manson 2013 · Hughes 2013 · Renova label

body.en: In the US, hot flashes, vaginal and vulvar symptoms and, for some products, bone loss. The 2025–26 label changes did not add skin.

For bothersome symptoms and bone, when started before 60 or within ten years of menopause, per the 2022 position statement. The large WHI trials do not support hormone therapy for preventing chronic disease.

title.en: What to decline, and what to offer

body.en: Compounded 'bioidentical' preparations lack efficacy and safety data, and over-the-counter 'hormone creams' are unapproved drugs under US rules. Daily sunscreen and a prescription retinoid have better evidence for the skin.

audioScript.en: Where does that leave hormone therapy for skin? In the United States, as of February 2026, the approved uses of menopausal hormone therapy are hot flashes, vaginal and vulvar symptoms, and for some products the prevention of bone loss. In late 2025 the FDA asked manufacturers to remove heart, breast cancer and dementia statements from the boxed warning, and it approved the first revised labels in February 2026. Skin still appears nowhere among the uses. The menopause society's 2022 position statement finds the balance favourable for symptoms and bone when therapy starts before sixty or within ten years of menopause, and it finds too little evidence for compounded bioidentical hormones. Low-dose vaginal estrogen for genitourinary symptoms is the one use aimed at the tissue itself. For the face, daily sunscreen and a prescription retinoid carry better evidence than any hormone. Treat symptoms on their merits, and count any skin change as a bonus.

prescriber.en: Prescribe hormone therapy for its labeled indications and the position statement's timing, and record that skin was discussed only as a secondary effect. Do not prescribe systemic or topical estrogen for wrinkles alone, and prefer FDA-approved products to compounded 'bioidentical' preparations.

clinical-staff.en: If a patient asks for 'hormones for my skin', ask about hot flashes, sleep and vaginal symptoms, record what she says, and route those symptoms to the prescriber. The skin concern stays with skin-directed care.

advisor.en: In the US, a cream sold as containing estrogen for the face is regulated as a drug, and compounded 'bioidentical' products lack efficacy and safety data. Menopausal symptoms are a conversation for a prescriber; sun protection is advice you can give.

body.en: One question to close lesson 2.2.

blocks.sourceNote: Lesson 2.2

prompt.en: A 52-year-old with no hot flashes, no sleep disturbance and no vaginal symptoms asks for estrogen 'to stop my face ageing'. What does the evidence support?

text.en: Estrogen rebuilds collagen, so hormone therapy is a reasonable anti-ageing choice.

why.en: That is the mechanism talking. Small trials show thicker skin, the largest trials found no difference in wrinkles, and skin is not an approved indication.

text.en: A compounded 'bioidentical' estrogen face cream avoids the risks of systemic therapy.

why.en: Compounded 'bioidentical' preparations lack efficacy and safety data and carry quality concerns; the menopause society says preference alone should not justify them.

text.en: Skin alone is not a reason to start hormone therapy; offer skin-directed care such as daily sunscreen and a retinoid, and revisit therapy if menopausal symptoms appear.

why.en: Correct. Symptoms decide hormone therapy. For skin, daily sunscreen has a large trial behind it and one tretinoin cream is FDA-approved as an adjunct for fine wrinkles.

feedback.en: Symptoms decide hormone therapy; skin gets skin-directed care.

title.en: Some syndromes show on the skin first.

body.en: A handful of inherited endocrine syndromes appear on the skin before the glands declare themselves. In multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN1), multiple facial angiofibromas and collagenomas are common. In Carney complex, lentigines on the lips, eyelids and canthi, blue naevi and small skin myxomas sit alongside myxomas of the heart and cortisol-secreting adrenal disease. In MEN2A, an itchy, rippled, pigmented plaque between the shoulder blades can precede medullary thyroid cancer.

points.en: MEN1: facial angiofibromas, collagenomas
Carney complex: lip and eyelid lentigines, myxomas
MEN2A: lichen amyloidosis between the shoulder blades

blocks.sourceNote: Darling 1997 · Kirschner 2000 · Correa 2015 · Stanescu 2024 · Lause 2017 · the guide's inherited-syndromes chapter

body.en: Loss of the tumour suppressor menin. Multiple facial angiofibromas, identical to those of tuberous sclerosis, and truncal collagenomas.
Inactivating variants in PRKAR1A, the regulatory subunit of protein kinase A. Lentigines, blue naevi and myxomas of skin and heart, with Cushing's syndrome from the adrenal.
Activating RET variants, most often at codon 634 when the skin is involved. Cutaneous lichen amyloidosis over the upper back, often found before the thyroid cancer.

audioScript.en: Some endocrine syndromes are written on the skin years before the glands give them away. In multiple endocrine neoplasia type one, most patients in one careful series had several facial angiofibromas, the same lesions seen in tuberous sclerosis, along with collagenomas on the trunk. In Carney complex, usually caused by inactivating variants in the PRKAR1A gene, freckle-like lentigines cluster on the lips, eyelids and the corners of the eyes, alongside blue naevi and small skin myxomas. The same patients can develop myxomas in the heart and cortisol-secreting adrenal disease. In MEN two A, an itchy, rippled, darkened patch between the shoulder blades, called cutaneous lichen amyloidosis, can appear long before medullary thyroid cancer. Each of these is a referral finding, and none of them is yours to diagnose alone.

body.en: In a consecutive series of 32 people with MEN1 examined at the US National Institutes of Health, 88% had multiple facial angiofibromas and 72% had collagenomas. The angiofibromas were clinically and histologically identical to those of tuberous sclerosis. The authors concluded that angiofibromas in someone without tuberous sclerosis call for biochemical testing for MEN1.

blocks.sourceNote: Darling et al., Arch Dermatol 1997

label.en: of 32 people with MEN1 had multiple facial angiofibromas

detail.en: Darling et al., 1997 — collagenomas in 72%

means.en: Multiple facial angiofibromas are common in MEN1 and can be its first visible sign; in someone without tuberous sclerosis they are a reason for endocrine testing, whatever the cosmetic plan.

doesNot.en: It does not mean a single facial papule is MEN1. This is one small referral-centre series, and angiofibromas have other causes, tuberous sclerosis above all.

body.en: Most endocrine skin signs you meet come from common disease. New generalised darkening, strongest in skin creases, scars, mucosa and sun-exposed skin, can signal primary adrenal insufficiency, which can turn into a life-threatening crisis. Hirsutism that appears fast, keeps progressing, or comes with a deepening voice or clitoromegaly makes an androgen-secreting tumour more likely. Velvety dark plaques of acanthosis nigricans track insulin resistance, pretibial myxoedema points to Graves' disease, and cold, dry skin suggests hypothyroidism.

points.en: Darkening in creases, scars and gums: adrenal insufficiency
Rapid hirsutism or virilization: exclude a tumour
Acanthosis, pretibial plaques, dry cool skin: metabolic and thyroid

blocks.sourceNote: Endocrine Society guidelines: Bornstein 2016, Martin 2018 · Lause 2017 · the guide's ch. 5 referral list

body.en: The hyperpigmentation of primary adrenal insufficiency favours sun-exposed skin, creases, mucosa and scars. In an acutely ill patient the guideline recommends testing, and a suspected crisis is treated before results return.
Rapid onset or progression of hirsutism, or signs of virilization, raise the likelihood of an androgen-secreting tumour; about 0.2% of hyperandrogenic women have one, and over half are malignant.
Acanthosis nigricans reflects hyperinsulinaemia; pretibial myxoedema reflects thyrotropin-receptor stimulation in Graves' disease; hypothyroid skin is cold and dry.

audioScript.en: Most of the endocrine skin signs you will actually meet come from common conditions. New, generalised darkening, most obvious in skin creases such as the palms, in scars, on the gums and on sun-exposed skin, can be the sign of primary adrenal insufficiency. In a patient who is also unwell, the Endocrine Society recommends testing, and a suspected adrenal crisis is treated before the results come back, because delay raises the risk of death. Hirsutism that arrives quickly, keeps progressing, or comes with a deeper voice or clitoromegaly makes an androgen-secreting tumour more likely, and more than half of those tumours are malignant. Velvety dark plaques in the neck folds track insulin resistance. Firm plaques on the shins point to Graves' disease, and cold, dry, coarse skin suggests an underactive thyroid. The skin shows you which door to knock on.

title.en: Where does this skin finding go?

body.en: Seven presentations from an aesthetic list, and three routes. Your job is to route the finding, not to make the diagnosis. The verdict and the source behind each appear as you answer.

blocks.sourceNote: Endocrine Society guidelines 2008, 2016, 2018 · Darling 1997 · Stanescu 2024 · the guide's ch. 5 referral list and algorithms

note.en: Findings that suggest a hormone-secreting tumour or an adrenal crisis
Findings that point to treatable or inherited endocrine disease

label.en: No endocrine flag on this alone

note.en: Common findings without discriminating features; reassess if others appear

callout.en: You route; the endocrinologist diagnoses.

prompt.en: One patient at a time: which route does this finding take?

label.en: Coarse chin and chest hair over four months; her voice has deepened

why.en: Rapid progression with virilization raises the likelihood of an androgen-secreting tumour, over half of which are malignant (Endocrine Society, 2018). The guide calls rapid virilization the one finding that demands urgent work-up.

label.en: Darkening of palm creases and gums, weight loss, feeling faint on standing

why.en: Hyperpigmentation with systemic symptoms suggests primary adrenal insufficiency; the guideline recommends testing in unwell patients and treating a suspected crisis without waiting for results.

label.en: Wide purple abdominal striae, easy bruising, trouble climbing stairs

why.en: Several discriminating features together: the guideline recommends testing for Cushing's syndrome, and the guide lists it for prompt endocrine referral.

label.en: Several facial angiofibromas, no tuberous sclerosis; her father had parathyroid surgery

why.en: Angiofibromas outside tuberous sclerosis call for biochemical testing for MEN1, and a relative with parathyroid disease strengthens the case.

label.en: Itchy, rippled brown patch between the shoulder blades; an aunt had thyroid cancer

why.en: Interscapular lichen amyloidosis clusters with RET variants in MEN2A and can precede medullary thyroid cancer; with that family history it needs endocrine and genetic assessment.

label.en: Puffy face after late nights; no bruising, striae or weakness

why.en: Facial fullness alone is a common, weakly discriminating feature, and the guideline advises against testing everyone. Reassess if discriminating features appear.

label.en: A few coarse hairs on the chin only; regular periods

why.en: The Endocrine Society suggests against androgen testing in women with regular cycles and unwanted local hair without an abnormal hirsutism score. Hair removal is a reasonable cosmetic choice.

done.en: Seven routed. Two need urgent assessment, three need an endocrine referral, and two can stay with skin-directed care.

body.en: A 29-year-old asks for laser removal of 'freckles' on her lips and at the corners of her eyes before her wedding. You notice a soft, skin-coloured papule on one eyelid. She mentions her father had 'a heart tumour' removed in his thirties. This is a fictional case built from the lesson's evidence; choose the first move that fits it.

points.en: Lip and canthal lentigines: typical of Carney complex
Eyelid papule: a possible cutaneous myxoma
A family heart tumour: the reason not to wait

blocks.sourceNote: Correa 2015 · Kirschner 2000 · the guide's inherited-syndromes chapter

body.en: Laser for lip and canthal 'freckles' before a fixed date.
Lentigines in a telling distribution, a soft eyelid papule, and a father with a heart tumour.
In Carney complex, cardiac myxomas cause more than half of deaths; suspicion is a reason for specialist assessment and screening.

setup.en: A 29-year-old asks for laser removal of 'freckles' on her lips and at the corners of her eyes before her wedding. You notice a soft, skin-coloured papule on one eyelid. She mentions her father had 'a heart tumour' removed in his thirties.

notice.en: Pigmentation at the inner or outer canthus is seen in Carney complex and Peutz–Jeghers syndrome
Cutaneous myxomas favour the eyelids, ears and nipples
Cardiac myxomas cause more than half of deaths in Carney complex

label.en: Proceed with the laser: lentigines are benign and she has a deadline.

why.en: The spots may well be benign. Their distribution, the eyelid papule and the family history are what matter, and together they flag a possible syndrome.

label.en: Pause the cosmetic plan, document the findings and family history, and refer her promptly for endocrine and genetic assessment.

why.en: Right. Canthal and lip lentigines with a possible myxoma and a family cardiac tumour fit Carney complex, where early echocardiographic screening matters. You route; the specialist diagnoses.

label.en: Order a cortisol test to check for Cushing's before deciding.

audioScript.en: Consider a fictional patient, built from this lesson's evidence. She is twenty-nine and wants the freckles on her lips and at the corners of her eyes lasered before her wedding. While you examine her you notice a soft, skin-coloured bump on one eyelid. She mentions that her father had a heart tumour removed in his thirties. Pigmented spots at the corners of the eyes are seen in Carney complex and Peutz–Jeghers syndrome, and small skin myxomas favour the eyelids and ears. In Carney complex, tumours of the heart cause more than half of the deaths, which is why screening matters once the diagnosis is suspected. The laser itself may be harmless. The question is what the skin is telling you. Choose your first move.

title.en: Metabolic, Adipose, and Incretin Axis Dynamics in Facial Architecture

summary.en: Dermal white adipose tissue (dWAT) biology; advanced glycation end products (AGEs) and inflammaging; the gut-skin neuroendocrine axis; incretin pharmacology; clinical management of rapid subcutaneous facial fat atrophy.

objective.en: By the end, you can evaluate the pathophysiology of dermal white adipose tissue, systemic inflammaging, and the facial structural consequences of GLP-1 and dual-incretin receptor agonist therapies.

title.en: Fat, incretins and the ageing face · three lessons

description.en: Lesson 3.1 Dermal fat and matrix glycation · Lesson 3.2 Incretin therapy and the changing face · Lesson 3.3 Gut barrier, endotoxaemia and inflammaging.

units.tutorContext: Module 3 teaches metabolic and adipose influences on facial architecture in four separate registers (mechanism, human evidence, regulatory status, open question). dWAT: distinct adipocyte layer in the reticular dermis; reactive adipogenesis and cathelicidin against S. aureus and its age-related loss via TGF-β are mouse data (D); human dWAT is cone-shaped around follicles and human acne lesions contain cathelicidin-producing preadipocytes (D); its role in human skin ageing is unmeasured. Facial subcutaneous fat sits in discrete compartments (cadaver anatomy); in 186 identical-twin pairs higher BMI looked older before ~40 and younger after (C, observational). Glycation: AGEs accumulate in human skin collagen (~5-fold from 20 to 85 y, up to 2x in type 1 diabetes; skin collagen half-life ~15 y) — C; AGE cross-links and RAGE–NF-κB causing visible ageing: the Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide rates B, the course grades D (lab/animal + associations); skin autofluorescence is a surrogate validated in non-pigmented skin; 'anti-glycation' products are tested on surrogates or appearance scores (guide grade C). Incretins: semaglutide (GLP-1 RA) and tirzepatide (GIP/GLP-1 RA). US status Sept 2026: Ozempic (T2D, 2017) and Wegovy (weight 06/2021; adolescents 12/2022; CV risk reduction 03/2024; MASH F2–F3 accelerated 08/2025); Mounjaro (T2D, 2022) and Zepbound (weight 11/2023; OSA 12/2024). Compounded, counterfeit and 'research' versions are not FDA-approved. STEP-1 −14.9% vs −2.4% (68 wk); SURMOUNT-1 −15.0 to −20.9% vs −3.1% (72 wk) — GRADE A for weight; median ~28% of weight lost is muscle-related (35 RCTs, B). Facial change ('Ozempic face'): retrospective imaging n=20, median 9% midface volume loss, mostly superficial, ~7%/10 kg (D); survey n=1,226, sagging/facial volume loss/hair loss rise with % weight lost (C); no RCT has measured the face; direct drug action on facial fat is a cell-study hypothesis. US labels list hair loss (~3–6% vs ~1% placebo, mostly women, linked to weight reduction) but not facial volume loss. Practice: counsel before treatment, photograph with consent, protect lean mass (protein, resistance training — no figures), refer restoration to a qualified aesthetic clinician; restoration advice is industry-linked expert consensus; decisions about stopping or changing the medicine belong to the prescriber and patient — never advise stopping, switching or dosing. Gut: inflammaging (IL-6/CRP predict frailty, death); metabolic endotoxaemia shown in mice and as a transient rise after a fatty meal in 12 men (D); restoring barrier function unproven for disease outside the gut; commercial zonulin ELISA detects other proteins. Probiotics for eczema: Cochrane 39 RCTs little/no patient-rated difference (B); children's meta-analysis small SCORAD gain (C). Rifaximin for rosacea with SIBO: small RCT (C). Tirzepatide + ixekizumab psoriasis: open-label Lilly phase 3b (C); liraglutide 20-person RCT negative (C); tirzepatide not approved for psoriasis in the US. Fibre: strong cardiometabolic evidence (guide grade A; review certainty moderate), no skin trials. Akkermansia pilot RCT metabolic only (C). 'Leaky gut' repair stack incl. BPC-157: guide grade D; BPC-157 not on the 503A bulks list (Sept 2026). Adapt the 'what you do next' to the learner's role (prescriber, clinical staff, advisor) without changing grades or regulatory facts. UK/EU status not yet mapped. No CME credit is currently offered.

learningObjectives.en: Analyze the endocrine and defensive functions of dWAT and the structural biomechanical damage induced by advanced glycation end products (AGEs).
Explain the biological mechanisms underlying rapid subcutaneous adipose depletion and skin laxity associated with GLP-1 and GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist therapies.
Appraise clinical trial data linking gut mucosal barrier permeability, metabolic endotoxemia, and cutaneous inflammatory dermatoses.

lead.en: Module 03 · Fat, incretins and the ageing face

title.en: The face changes when the fat does.

body.en: Facial shape depends on fat as much as on collagen. In three lessons you will separate what is known about the skin's own fat, sugar damage to the dermis, weight-loss drugs and the gut from what is still mechanism, marketing or an open question.

points.en: 3.1 Dermal fat and sugar damage to collagen
3.2 Semaglutide, tirzepatide and the changing face
3.3 The gut barrier, endotoxaemia and inflammaging

blocks.sourceNote: Hormones and Peptides for Skin · Module 03

title.en: The skin keeps its own fat.

body.en: Beneath the dermis lies subcutaneous fat. Within the reticular dermis itself sits a thinner layer, dermal white adipose tissue. In mice, this layer expands rapidly after a Staphylococcus aureus infection, its new fat cells release the antimicrobial peptide cathelicidin, and the capacity fades with age through TGF-β signalling. Human skin arranges this fat differently, in cones around hair follicles, and human acne lesions contain perifollicular preadipocytes that make cathelicidin. What the layer contributes to human skin ageing has not been measured.

points.en: A second fat layer inside the dermis
In mice: antimicrobial, and lost with age
In people: a different shape, and an open question about ageing

blocks.sourceNote: Zhang 2015, 2019 · Chen 2019 · Kruglikov & Scherer 2016 · O'Neill 2022 · Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, ch. 11

body.en: Dermal white adipose tissue sits inside the reticular dermis, separate from the subcutaneous fat below. Fat as a whole is an endocrine organ that releases hormones such as leptin and adiponectin.
The layer expands after skin infection and its fat cells release cathelicidin. Older mice lose much of this capacity, through TGF-β signalling.
Human dermal fat clusters in cones around hair follicles, and acne lesions contain preadipocytes that make cathelicidin. Its part in skin ageing is unmeasured.

audioScript.en: Most people picture skin fat as one layer under the dermis. There is a second, thinner layer inside the reticular dermis itself, called dermal white adipose tissue. In mice, this layer expands rapidly after a Staphylococcus aureus infection, and its new fat cells release cathelicidin, an antimicrobial peptide. Older mice lose much of that capacity, through TGF-beta signalling. Human skin arranges this fat differently, in small cones around hair follicles, and human acne lesions contain preadipocytes around the follicle that make cathelicidin. What the layer contributes to human skin ageing has not yet been measured. So hold two things apart when you hear about skin fat. The defence story is strong in mice and emerging in people. The ageing story in people is still a proposal.

title.en: Fat that holds the face up.

body.en: Cadaver dissection shows that the face's subcutaneous fat sits in separate compartments, and facial ageing is partly how each compartment changes. Weight shows the same thing from the outside. In a study of 186 pairs of identical twins, the twin with the higher body-mass index looked older before about age 40 and younger after it.

blocks.sourceNote: Rohrich & Pessa 2007 · Guyuron 2009

label.en: pairs of identical twins compared for facial ageing

detail.en: Guyuron et al., 2009 — a four-point higher BMI tracked with an older look before about 40 and a younger look after it

means.en: From midlife on, facial fat goes with a younger-looking face. That fits the anatomy: the face ages partly as its fat compartments change. GRADE C, observational.

doesNot.en: It is an observational comparison of photographs. It does not show that gaining weight rejuvenates, or that fat loss on a drug changes the skin itself.

body.en: Glycation is a slow, non-enzymatic reaction. Reducing sugars attach to protein amino groups, rearrange into Amadori products and end as advanced glycation end products, or AGEs. On long-lived dermal collagen, AGEs form cross-links that stiffen the matrix. Through their receptor, RAGE, AGEs switch on inflammatory signalling in laboratory studies. The Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide rates the structural and inflammatory effects B; the course grades the causal link to visible ageing D, because the human data are associations.

points.en: Sugar + protein → Schiff base → Amadori product → AGE
Cross-links stiffen long-lived collagen
RAGE signalling: shown in the laboratory

blocks.sourceNote: Gkogkolou & Böhm 2012 · Dyer 1993 · Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, ch. 13

body.en: Reducing sugars bind protein amino groups, form a reversible Schiff base, then a more stable Amadori product, and finally irreversible AGEs.
Structural: AGEs cross-link collagen and elastin and stiffen the dermis. Signalling: AGEs bind RAGE, which drives NF-κB and inflammatory cytokines in cell and animal studies.
The Hormonaly endocrinology guide rates both B. The course grades the causal link to visible ageing D, because the human data are associations.

audioScript.en: Glycation is chemistry before it is biology. Reducing sugars attach to the amino groups of proteins, rearrange into more stable products, and end as advanced glycation end products, known as AGEs. Dermal collagen lasts for years, so it collects AGEs, and they form cross-links that make the matrix stiffer. AGEs also bind a receptor called RAGE, which in laboratory studies switches on inflammatory signalling and enzymes that break down matrix. Keep the registers apart here. The chemistry, and the build-up of AGEs in human skin, are well documented. The idea that AGEs cause the wrinkles and laxity you see in clinic rests on laboratory and animal work plus human associations. The Aesthetic and Regenerative Endocrinology guide rates the structural and inflammatory effects grade B. This course grades the causal link D, and the next moment shows why.

title.en: Fifteen years on the same collagen.

body.en: Human skin collagen turns over slowly; tissue analysis puts its half-life at about 15 years. In skin biopsies, glycoxidation products in collagen rose about five-fold between ages 20 and 85, and were up to twice as high in type 1 diabetes. Skin autofluorescence, a non-invasive reading, correlates moderately with those biopsy measures and was validated in non-pigmented skin.

blocks.sourceNote: Verzijl 2000 · Dyer 1993 · Meerwaldt 2004

label.en: estimated half-life of human skin collagen

detail.en: Verzijl et al., 2000 · AGE content of skin collagen rises about five-fold from age 20 to 85 (Dyer et al., 1993)

means.en: Glycation damage accumulates on the same collagen for years, and faster with higher glucose exposure. That much is measured in human skin: direct, observational, GRADE C.

doesNot.en: It does not show how much of visible ageing AGEs cause, or that any product reverses established cross-links. Skin autofluorescence is a surrogate reading of AGE load.

body.en: Six statements you will hear about skin fat and glycation. Before you see where each one stands, decide what kind of evidence is behind it.

prompt.en: Tap what stands behind each statement.

label.en: Dermal fat cells release cathelicidin to fight Staphylococcus aureus

why.en: Shown in mouse infection models (D). Human acne lesions contain preadipocytes that make cathelicidin, but protection against infection has not been tested in people.

label.en: Dermal fat loses its defensive capacity with age

why.en: Shown in mice, through TGF-β signalling (D). The equivalent change in human skin has not been measured.

label.en: AGEs build up in skin collagen with age, faster in diabetes

why.en: Measured directly in human skin biopsies (C, observational), and up to twice as high in type 1 diabetes.

label.en: Skin collagen stays in place for many years

why.en: Human tissue analysis puts the half-life of skin collagen at about 15 years (C), which is why glycation damage accumulates.

label.en: AGEs drive skin inflammation through their receptor, RAGE

why.en: Laboratory and animal work. The Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide rates it B; the course grades the causal link D because the human data are associations.

label.en: An anti-glycation serum reverses cross-linked collagen

why.en: Not shown. Trials of 'anti-glycation' products measure surrogate readings or appearance scores; none found for this course measured cross-links in human skin. The guide rates the evidence for these products C, on surrogate endpoints.

done.en: Six sorted. Two are measured in human skin, three come from mice or cells, and one has no study behind it.

body.en: One question to close lesson 3.1.

blocks.sourceNote: Lesson 3.1

prompt.en: A patient shows you her skin autofluorescence reading, lower after eight weeks on an 'anti-glycation' supplement. What does that result show?

text.en: The supplement has reversed glycation damage in her dermis.

why.en: A lower surrogate reading is not a measurement of collagen cross-links, and the device was validated in non-pigmented skin.

text.en: A change in a surrogate marker; it shows nothing yet about collagen cross-links, how her skin looks or how it ages.

why.en: Correct. The surrogate moved; the outcome is unknown.

text.en: Nothing at all, because glycation does not happen in human skin.

why.en: It does: AGEs accumulate in human skin collagen with age and faster in diabetes. The question is what the product changed.

feedback.en: A surrogate reading is where the evidence starts, never where it ends.

body.en: GLP-1 and GIP are incretins, hormones the gut releases after a meal that amplify glucose-dependent insulin release; GLP-1 also slows gastric emptying and reduces appetite. Native GLP-1 is broken down within minutes. Semaglutide is a long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist, and tirzepatide activates both GIP and GLP-1 receptors. In the US, as of September 2026, both are FDA-approved drugs for defined indications, set out in the next moment.

points.en: Incretins amplify insulin after meals
Semaglutide: GLP-1 receptor agonist
Tirzepatide: GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist

blocks.sourceNote: Drucker 2018 · Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, ch. 12 · Peptide Pocket Guide · US labels

body.en: GLP-1 from intestinal L-cells and GIP from K-cells amplify insulin release when glucose is high. GLP-1 also slows the stomach and reduces appetite.
Native GLP-1 is cleared within minutes by the enzyme DPP-4. The drug molecules are modified to last far longer in the blood.
Semaglutide is sold as Ozempic and Wegovy, tirzepatide as Mounjaro and Zepbound. The brand tells you the approved use.

audioScript.en: After a meal, the gut releases two hormones called incretins, GLP-1 and GIP. Both amplify insulin release when glucose is high, and GLP-1 also slows the stomach and reduces appetite. Native GLP-1 lasts only minutes in the blood before an enzyme breaks it down, so the drug molecules are engineered to last far longer. Semaglutide activates the GLP-1 receptor. Tirzepatide activates both the GIP and the GLP-1 receptors. Those are the mechanisms. The regulatory facts sit in a separate register. In the United States, as of September 2026, both molecules are FDA-approved drugs, sold under one brand name for type 2 diabetes and another for chronic weight management, with further indications for the heart, the liver and sleep apnoea. The face appears nowhere on those labels, and that is where this lesson begins.

body.en: The facial changes in this lesson happen to people taking approved drugs for approved reasons. Know the indications, and their dates, before you discuss the side effects. Status below is for the US, from FDA records checked in September 2026; UK and EU status is being mapped for this course.

blocks.sourceNote: US labels via DailyMed (2026) · Drugs@FDA · FDA, current 1 Sep 2026 · Ashraf 2024

note.en: First approved 2017. The label adds cardiovascular and kidney risk reduction in people with type 2 diabetes.

Approved June 2021; adolescents from age 12 added December 2022. Cardiovascular risk reduction in established heart disease with obesity or overweight, March 2024. MASH with moderate to advanced liver fibrosis, accelerated approval, August 2025.
First approved 2022. The label adds cardiovascular risk reduction in type 2 diabetes at high risk.
Approved November 2023. Moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnoea with obesity, December 2024.

FDA warns about compounded, counterfeit and falsely labelled 'research' semaglutide and tirzepatide (page current 1 September 2026). Semaglutide bought online without a prescription has failed independent testing.

callout.en: Approved for diabetes, weight, the heart, the liver and sleep apnoea. The face is on none of these labels.

title.en: Large trials, measured on the scale.

body.en: In STEP-1, 1,961 adults without diabetes lost a mean 14.9% of body weight on semaglutide over 68 weeks, against 2.4% on placebo. In SURMOUNT-1, 2,539 adults lost 15.0% to 20.9% on tirzepatide over 72 weeks, depending on dose, against 3.1% on placebo. Both Hormonaly guides grade weight management A. Across 35 randomized trials of incretin drugs, a median of about 28% of the weight lost was muscle-related tissue.

blocks.sourceNote: Wilding 2021 · Jastreboff 2022 · Batsis 2026

label.en: mean weight loss in STEP-1 (semaglutide, 68 weeks) and SURMOUNT-1 (tirzepatide, highest dose, 72 weeks)

detail.en: Placebo 2.4% and 3.1% · both trials industry-funded, both the basis for approval

means.en: These drugs produce large, reproducible weight loss in randomized trials: GRADE A for the approved indications. Part of what is lost is lean tissue, which is why the Hormonaly guide pairs treatment with protein and resistance training.

doesNot.en: Neither pivotal trial measured facial fat, skin laxity or appearance. An A for weight loss says nothing about the face.

body.en: The phrase bundles four kinds of statement. Kept apart, they tell a patient far more than the headline does.

blocks.sourceNote: Sharma 2025 · Rao 2026 · Daneshgaran 2025 · US labels 2026 · Paschou 2025

note.en: Losing fat deflates the superficial facial compartments and unmasks laxity that was already there.

value.en: Observational and small: C to D

note.en: One imaging study of 20 patients found a median 9% loss of midface volume, mostly superficial, about 7% per 10 kg lost. A survey of 1,226 patients found sagging, facial volume loss and hair shedding reported more often the more weight was lost. A systematic review of the plastic-surgery literature found it limited by study bias. No randomized trial has measured the face.

value.en: Hair loss labelled; facial change unlisted

note.en: Both labels list hair loss (about 3–6% on drug against about 1% on placebo, mostly in women, linked to weight reduction). The semaglutide label also lists altered skin sensation. Facial volume loss is not a labelled adverse reaction.
Whether these drugs act on facial fat or skin cells beyond the effect of weight loss rests on cell studies and has not been tested in people.

callout.en: So far, the evidence ties facial change to how much weight is lost.

title.en: Counsel before, record during, refer when asked.

body.en: Raise facial volume change and hair shedding before treatment starts; the Hormonaly guide advises this especially for older patients. During treatment, photograph the face with consent, and support the protein intake and resistance training the guide recommends to protect lean mass. When a patient wants the face restored, refer to a qualified aesthetic or dermatology colleague. Published advice on restoration is expert opinion, the main consensus statement was developed with industry involvement, and randomized trials of fillers and devices in these patients are registered without results. Decisions about the medicine itself stay with the prescriber and the patient.

points.en: Before: set expectations about face and hair
During: photographs with consent, protect lean mass
When asked: refer for restoration

blocks.sourceNote: Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, ch. 12, 14 · Nikolis 2025 · ClinicalTrials.gov, checked 24 Sep 2026

body.en: Name facial volume change and hair shedding as possibilities, especially with older patients, and record that you did.
Photograph the face with consent so change is measured, and support protein intake and resistance training to protect lean mass.
Refer restoration requests to a qualified colleague. Published advice is expert opinion, and the randomized trials of fillers and devices have not reported.

audioScript.en: Three moments matter in practice. Before treatment starts, raise facial volume change and hair shedding as possibilities, especially with older patients, as the Hormonaly guide advises, and record that you did. During treatment, photograph the face with consent so that change is measured rather than remembered, and support the protein intake and resistance training the guide recommends to protect lean mass. When a patient asks for help with the face, refer to a qualified aesthetic or dermatology colleague. The published advice on restoring volume after drug-driven weight loss is expert opinion, the main consensus statement was developed with industry involvement, and randomized trials of fillers and devices in these patients are registered with no results yet. Whatever your role, decisions about the medicine itself stay with the prescriber and the patient.

prescriber.en: Put facial volume change and hair shedding into the consent conversation before you start, and document it. At follow-up, review nutrition, strength training and consented photographs. Keep the indication in view, and refer restoration requests rather than improvising them.

clinical-staff.en: Record the patient's concern, the medicine and who prescribes it, and consented photographs. Do not suggest pausing or changing the medicine; bring the concern to the prescriber and pass restoration questions to the aesthetic lead.

advisor.en: Explain that facial change tracks the weight lost and that hair loss is a listed side effect. Questions about the dose or about stopping belong with the prescriber; restoration questions belong with a qualified aesthetic clinician.

title.en: Ten months in, and unhappy with the mirror.

body.en: A 58-year-old patient has taken semaglutide for obesity for ten months, prescribed by her physician, and has lost 18% of her body weight. Her blood pressure and glucose have improved. She is distressed by hollow cheeks, new laxity along the jaw and more hair in her brush, and asks whether she should stop the injections. This is a fictional case built from the lesson's evidence; there is one right first move.

points.en: Facial volume loss tracks the weight lost
Hair loss is a labelled side effect, more common in women
The indication is responding; the medicine decision is the prescriber's

blocks.sourceNote: Sharma 2025 · Rao 2026 · Wegovy label 2026 · Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, ch. 12

setup.en: A 58-year-old patient has taken semaglutide for obesity for ten months, prescribed by her physician, and has lost 18% of her body weight. Her blood pressure and glucose have improved. She is distressed by hollow cheeks, new laxity along the jaw and more hair in her brush, and asks whether she should stop the injections.

notice.en: Facial volume loss in the studies so far tracks the amount of weight lost
Hair loss is listed on the US label, more often in women, and linked to weight reduction
The drug was prescribed for an indication that is responding

label.en: Tell her to stop the injections; her face matters more than the scale.

why.en: That is a medication decision made on one side effect, outside her prescriber's care, and it sets aside an indication that is working.

why.en: Right. Counsel, record, refer. The medicine decision stays with her prescriber, and restoration goes to someone qualified to provide it.

audioScript.en: Picture a fifty-eight-year-old patient, fictional and built from this lesson's evidence. She has taken semaglutide for obesity for ten months, prescribed by her physician, and has lost eighteen percent of her body weight. Her blood pressure and glucose have improved. She is distressed by hollow cheeks and new looseness along the jaw, and she is finding more hair in her brush. She asks whether she should stop the injections. Consider what the evidence says. In the studies so far, facial volume loss tracks the amount of weight lost. Hair loss is a labelled side effect, reported more often in women and linked to weight reduction. The drug was prescribed for a medical reason, and that reason is going well. Decide how you would answer her.

prescriber.en: You own the medication conversation: review her progress against the indication, her nutrition, strength training and hair, and refer for restoration if she wants it. Document the discussion.

clinical-staff.en: You record the concern, consented photographs and the hair change, and bring it to the prescriber this week. You do not advise on the dose or on stopping.

advisor.en: You explain what is known, suggest she talk to her prescriber before changing anything, and point her to a qualified aesthetic clinician for restoration questions.

body.en: Inflammaging is the chronic, low-grade, sterile inflammation that rises with age. In older adults, higher IL-6 and CRP predict frailty and death. One proposed source is the gut. body.en: A slow rise in background inflammation with age. Higher IL-6 and CRP predict frailty, disability and death in older adults.
Bacterial lipopolysaccharide crossing a leaky barrier is one proposed source, shown in mice and as a short rise after a fatty meal in a small human study.

audioScript.en: Ageing brings a slow rise in background inflammation, called inflammaging. It is low-grade and sterile, and in older adults higher IL-6 and C-reactive protein predict frailty, disability and death. One proposed source is the gut. In mice, a high-fat diet raises bacterial lipopolysaccharide in the blood, and infusing that endotoxin reproduces weight gain and insulin resistance. In twelve healthy men, a single high-fat meal raised plasma endotoxin within four hours. That is the mechanism usually called metabolic endotoxaemia, or leaky gut. The human evidence stops short of the skin. Measuring gut permeability is difficult, and a leading review concludes that it is still unproven whether restoring the barrier improves disease outside the gut. Hold that line as you look at what patients are sold.

title.en: Thirty-nine trials of probiotics for eczema.

body.en: An independent Cochrane review pooled 39 randomized trials, with 2,599 participants, of oral probiotics for eczema. Probiotics probably make little or no difference to patient-rated symptoms, and investigator-rated severity fell by less than the minimum clinically important difference. A 2024 European task-force meta-analysis in children without food allergy reported a significant fall in severity scores.

audioScript.en: Patients often link their skin to their gut. Start where the evidence is. Diet quality, treatment of metabolic disease and the established treatment for the skin condition itself all come first. Be careful with tests. A widely used commercial zonulin assay was shown to detect proteins other than zonulin, so a result cannot tell you whether a gut is leaky. Be careful with products too. Probiotics are strain-specific, and their effects on eczema are small at best. The Hormonaly guide gives the popular gut-repair stack of glutamine, zinc carnosine and BPC-157 a grade of D. As of September 2026, in the United States, BPC-157 remains off the 503A bulks list after the July advisory-committee review. Investigational peptides come last, if at all. Whatever your role, name the evidence type before you name the product.

prescriber.en: Treat the skin disease on its own evidence and metabolic disease directly. A zonulin result should not guide care. In the US, BPC-157 has no 503A bulks-list standing as of September 2026, so compounding it for gut repair is not an option.

clinical-staff.en: If a patient brings a gut-repair kit or a zonulin result, record the products and the result and bring them to the prescriber. Do not interpret the test or advise on the products.

advisor.en: You can say that fibre-rich diets have strong evidence for metabolic health, that probiotics are strain-specific with small skin effects at best, and that injected or research peptides need a prescriber.

units.tutorContext: Module 4 teaches evidence appraisal of skin peptides in four separate registers (mechanism, human evidence, regulatory status, open question). Topical GHK-Cu: plausible copper-enzyme mechanism from originator reviews; one indexed RCT (Miller 2006, post-laser healing) plus sponsor-run cosmetic trials; GRADE C; injectable use has no RCTs and commonly irritates; US 503A Category 1 for non-injectable routes only (FDA list 14 May 2026; PCAC consultation planned by end Feb 2027). pal-KTTKS and Argireline: C (sponsor RCTs plus independent Aruan 2023); Matrixyl 3000, SNAP-8, Leuphasyl: D (no randomized trial; manufacturer data, plus one small uncontrolled university volunteer study for Leuphasyl). Oral collagen: pooled RCTs positive but Myung 2025 finds no effect in unfunded or high-quality trials; dietary supplement in the US. BPC-157: rodent + case series, no published human efficacy RCT (Sept 2026); TB-500 is the Tβ4 17-23 fragment, never trialled; KPV mouse colitis only; LL-37 small positive RCT then negative phase IIb. PCAC reviewed BPC-157/KPV/TB-500 in July 2026 — advisory only; not on the 503A bulks list. Never give doses, stacks, reconstitution or sourcing advice; name the route and the grade; route injected or research-use-only products to a prescriber; adapt the 'what you do next' to the learner's role (prescriber, clinical staff, advisor) without changing grades or regulatory facts. No CME credit is currently offered.

title.en: A plasma tripeptide with a copper habit.

body.en: GHK is a tripeptide found in human plasma, first described in 1973. Bound to copper it becomes GHK-Cu, which is proposed to deliver copper to enzymes such as superoxide dismutase and lysyl oxidase and to switch on wound-healing and antioxidant gene programmes. Most of that mechanistic literature comes from the group that discovered the peptide.

points.en: Endogenous: GHK circulates in human plasma
Proposed: copper delivery to matrix and antioxidant enzymes
Mechanism register only — written largely by the originator

blocks.sourceNote: Pickart & Thaler 1973 · Pickart 2008, 2015, 2018 · Peptide Pocket Guide

body.en: GHK — glycyl-histidyl-lysine — was isolated from human plasma in 1973. It binds copper readily, and the copper complex is what the skin-care literature calls GHK-Cu.

title.en: What it is proposed to do

body.en: The proposed mechanism is copper delivery to enzymes that build and protect the matrix, plus broad changes in gene expression linked to wound healing.
Much of this work, including the gene-expression reviews, comes from the peptide's discoverer. That does not make it wrong. It does make it a mechanism, and it is worth saying who proposed it.

audioScript.en: Start with the molecule. GHK is a three-amino-acid peptide that circulates in human plasma; it was first described in 1973. It binds copper readily, and the copper complex, GHK-Cu, is what skin-care labels mean when they say copper peptide. The proposed mechanism is that GHK-Cu delivers copper to enzymes that build and protect the dermal matrix, such as lysyl oxidase and superoxide dismutase, and shifts gene expression toward wound healing. Two things to hold on to. First, this is a mechanism, which explains why the peptide might work and leaves open whether it does. Second, most of this literature was written by the group that discovered the peptide. Keep both in mind when you reach the trials.

body.en: A search of PubMed in September 2026 found one randomized controlled trial of topical GHK-Cu in human skin: 2006, healing after CO₂ laser resurfacing. The cosmetic trials cited for anti-ageing claims are manufacturer-sponsored and not indexed. Both Hormonaly guides grade topical use C.

label.en: indexed randomized trial of topical GHK-Cu in human skin

detail.en: Miller et al., 2006 — healing after CO₂ laser resurfacing, not photoageing

means.en: The human evidence for topical GHK-Cu is small: one small indexed trial plus sponsor-run cosmetic studies. GRADE C is the honest ceiling.

doesNot.en: It does not show that GHK-Cu fails, that it treats photoageing, or anything about injecting it. A thin evidence base is an unknown, not a negative.

body.en: Every peptide question has four separate answers. For GHK-Cu they point in different directions, which is exactly why they must not be blended into one sentence.

audioScript.en: Here is what that means in the room. Topical GHK-Cu is a reasonable cosmetic conversation, as long as you describe the evidence honestly: small trials, modest effects, grade C. Injected GHK-Cu is not the same product in a stronger form. There are no randomized trials of injection, injection-site pain and rash are common because copper irritates tissue, and in the United States the injectable route sits outside the Category 1 listing that covers non-injectable use. title.en: Three families, one question: who ran the trial?

body.en: Signal peptides such as palmitoyl pentapeptide-4 (pal-KTTKS, Matrixyl) are meant to tell fibroblasts to make matrix. SNAP-25 mimics — Argireline, its longer cousin SNAP-8, and Leuphasyl — are meant to quieten expression lines. Oral collagen peptides are swallowed, not applied. All three families have a trial record, and in all three the question that matters most is who funded it.

points.en: Signal peptides: 'make more matrix'
SNAP-25 mimics: 'relax the line'
Oral collagen: the supplement aisle

blocks.sourceNote: Lupo & Cole 2007 · Lintner & Peschard 2000 · Blanes-Mira 2002 · Errante 2020

body.en: Palmitoylated fragments of matrix proteins, designed to mimic the signals that tell fibroblasts to repair. The palmitoyl tail helps them into the skin.
Argireline copies the end of SNAP-25, a protein botulinum toxin cleaves. SNAP-8 is the maker's eight-residue extension. The premise is a gentler topical version of the same effect.
Hydrolysed collagen taken by mouth, sold as a supplement, with more randomized trials than any topical peptide — and the clearest funding problem.

audioScript.en: Lesson two covers three families that fill the cosmetic and supplement shelves. Signal peptides, like palmitoyl pentapeptide-4, sold as Matrixyl, are fragments of matrix proteins meant to tell fibroblasts to make more collagen. SNAP-25 mimics, Argireline and its longer cousin SNAP-8, copy part of a nerve-terminal protein that botulinum toxin targets; the idea is a gentle, topical version of that effect. And oral collagen peptides are swallowed, not applied. Every one of these has trials behind it. As you go through them, keep asking one question before any other: who ran the trial, and who paid for it.

why.en: GRADE C. A 12-week split-face RCT in 93 women, funded by the manufacturer, and an independent 2023 RCT.
GRADE D. Only the maker's technical dossier, which is not indexed.

GRADE C in this course. Placebo-controlled RCTs, including an independent head-to-head trial, show modest effects. The two Hormonaly guides disagree (C in Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, D in the Peptide Pocket Guide); the trials decide it here.
GRADE D. Its efficacy figures come from the manufacturer, and the indexed studies test it mixed with other actives, so none isolates it.
GRADE D. The maker's studies, an in-vitro synergy figure and one small uncontrolled university volunteer study (2014); no randomized trial.

title.en: Twenty-three trials, split by who paid.

body.en: Pooled, oral collagen trials show better hydration, elasticity and wrinkle scores, and the Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide grades them C. A 2025 meta-analysis split the same kind of trials by funding and by quality. The benefit appeared only in pharmaceutical-funded and low-quality trials. Unfunded and high-quality trials showed no effect.

blocks.sourceNote: Myung & Park, Am J Med 2025 · Pu 2023 · de Miranda 2021 · Kim 2018

label.en: in the 2025 meta-analysis that split oral-collagen trials by funding and quality

detail.en: 1,474 participants

means.en: The pooled benefit of oral collagen disappears when you look only at independent or high-quality trials. The course keeps the guide's GRADE C and shows why a downgrade has been proposed to its author.

doesNot.en: It does not show collagen is harmful, and it does not rule out benefit for an individual. It is a statement about the evidence, and it says nothing about topical peptides.

body.en: In the US, cosmetic peptides are cosmetic ingredients, not drugs, and their safety is assessed under a cosmetics framework. Oral collagen is a dietary supplement: it may not claim to treat disease, and product quality and content vary. Neither route has to prove efficacy before sale — which is why the funding question matters.

Dietary supplement: no disease claims; quality varies

audioScript.en: Now the regulatory register, stated for the United States. Cosmetic peptides are cosmetic ingredients, not drugs; their safety is assessed under a cosmetics framework, and nobody has to prove they work before they are sold. Oral collagen is sold as a dietary supplement, so it cannot claim to treat a disease, and what is in the tub varies from brand to brand. That is the whole reason the funding question matters here. When no regulator asks for efficacy, the only efficacy data are the trials someone chose to pay for. UK and EU rules are being mapped for this course and will be added.

prescriber.en: Nothing here needs a prescription. If you recommend a product, recommend it on evidence, name the grade, and disclose any relationship with the brand. The 'topical Botox' claim is not one to repeat.

advisor.en: The claim you can stand behind is modest, small-trial evidence. Supplements cannot be sold as treating a disease; if a patient expects collagen to fix a skin condition, that is a conversation for a prescriber.

audioScript.en: Lesson three moves from the cosmetic shelf to the peptides patients buy online and inject. BPC-157 is a fifteen-residue peptide first described in 1993. Its evidence is a large rodent literature, most of it from one research group, and uncontrolled human case series. TB-500 is sold as thymosin, but when anti-doping chemists analysed the product they found a seven-residue fragment, residues seventeen to twenty-three of thymosin beta-four. That fragment has never been tested in a trial. KPV is the last three amino acids of alpha-MSH; it calms inflammation in mouse colitis models, and there is no randomized human trial of it for anything. All three have plausible mechanisms, and none has a controlled human trial.

body.en: As of September 2026 no randomized efficacy trial of BPC-157 in people has been published in full. FDA's July 2026 briefing found one randomized, placebo-controlled trial reported only as a 2005 meeting abstract: 53 people with ulcerative colitis, two weeks of treatment, and no significant difference from placebo. ClinicalTrials.gov adds a 2015 phase 1 safety study that never posted results, a completed 2025 single-arm product study with no results posted, and a randomized phase 1 trial after rotator-cuff surgery due to start in 2027.

summary.en: Hair follicle neuroendocrine regulation, immune privilege collapse, and cycling; melanocortin receptor pharmacology (MC1R-MC5R); afamelanotide indications; Melanotan II systemic toxicity and oncologic risk; experimental hair peptides (PTD-DBM, Zinc Thymulin).

title.en: Follicle, pigment and melanocortins · three lessons

description.en: Lesson 5.1 The hair follicle as an endocrine mini-organ · Lesson 5.2 Afamelanotide, Melanotan II and the melanocortin receptors · Lesson 5.3 Investigational hair peptides, graded.

units.tutorContext: Module 5 teaches the hair follicle and the melanocortin system in four separate registers (mechanism, human evidence, regulatory status, open question). Follicle: ex vivo human scalp follicles run an HPA-like loop (CRH → POMC products → cortisol, with feedback) and a GH/IGF-1-like loop (D, organ culture, Paus group); local DHT miniaturises susceptible follicles (androgenetic alopecia); anagen immune-privilege collapse underlies alopecia areata. Baricitinib: BRAVE-AA1/AA2, 1,200 adults, SALT ≤20 at week 36 in up to 39% on baricitinib vs 3–6% on placebo; FDA-approved 13 Jun 2022 for adults with severe alopecia areata (A). A&RE hair-loss workup: patterned → AGA (topical minoxidil; finasteride in men); diffuse after trigger → telogen effluvium (reassure, ferritin, TSH); patchy smooth ± nail pitting → alopecia areata (dermatology referral, thyroid/autoimmune screen); androgen excess → work-up; ferritin + TSH always; scarring → biopsy; refer severe or rapid AA promptly. Minoxidil (men and women) and finasteride (men): A by RCT meta-analysis (Adil 2017); US: topical minoxidil OTC (approved 1988), finasteride Rx (1997). Melanocortins: skin makes POMC → ACTH, α-MSH, β-endorphin; MC1R pigment, MC2R adrenal, MC3R/MC4R brain (appetite; central sexual effects), MC5R sebum. Afamelanotide: MC1R agonist; two sponsor-funded phase 3 RCTs in EPP (US median 69.4 vs 40.8 pain-free sunlight hours; EU 6.0 vs 0.8); EU authorised 22 Dec 2014 (exceptional circumstances), US 2019; EPP only, manufacturer's implant; US label (Aug 2024) recommends full-body skin examination twice yearly; A for EPP; vitiligo phase 3 has no posted results. Melanotan II: non-selective MC1R/3R/4R/5R agonist, brain-penetrant; only controlled data a 3-man 1996 pilot and a 10-man 1998 ED crossover; guides disagree (Pocket Guide C, A&RE D) — course grades cosmetic use D; case-report harms: darkening/growing and eruptive atypical naevi, melanonychia, ≥5 melanomas all with other risk factors (causation unproven), ischaemic priapism, sympathomimetic toxicity with rhabdomyolysis, PRES; online vials held 43–88% of the label with impurities. Status: approved for no indication; US FDA compounding page (22 Apr 2026) lists it among withdrawn category-2 nominations with safety risks; UK MHRA (17 Apr 2024) injectables are unauthorised medicines, stop immediately; Australia TGA (17 Aug 2026) prescription-only, no ARTG product, not approved for tanning; EU status not asserted. A&RE: personal or family history of melanoma = absolute contraindication. A patient disclosing use: stop, record product and seller, full skin and nail examination with dermoscopy/baseline photos where available, prompt dermatology referral; never offer afamelanotide as a substitute. PTD-DBM: CXXC5–Dishevelled decoy activating Wnt; one 2017 mouse/tissue study from the developer's group; no human trial published or registered (Sept 2026); D; theoretical off-target Wnt cancer concern untested. Zinc thymulin: zinc-dependent thymic nonapeptide; no indexed human hair study; D. US (14 May 2026): thymulin acetate 503A Category 3; PTD-DBM on no list; neither on the bulks list (21 CFR 216.23). Never give doses, regimens, reconstitution, sourcing or administration advice; adapt the 'what you do next' to the learner's role (prescriber, clinical staff, advisor) without changing grades or regulatory facts. No CME credit is currently offered.

learningObjectives.en: Explain how peripheral endocrine signaling, steroid conversions, and immune privilege collapse regulate follicular cycling and alopecia phenotypes.
Compare the verified indications of FDA-approved afamelanotide with the severe systemic, dysplastic, and melanocytic risks of unregulated Melanotan II.
Appraise mechanistic claims and preliminary data for experimental follicular agents such as PTD-DBM and Zinc Thymulin against guideline-directed alopecia standards.

In three lessons you will see how the follicle and the pigment system run on the skin's own hormones, why one melanocortin drug is approved while its gray-market cousin is approved nowhere, and how to grade the hair peptides patients bring to you.
